stem: A cyclist speeding at 18 km h −1 on a level road takes a sharp circular turn of radius 3 m without reducing the speed and without bending towards the centre of the circular path. The coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the road is 0.1. Will the cyclist slip while taking the turn? —
book_key: Yes — the cyclist slips (v² = 25 > μrg = 3 m²s −2 )

stem: Find the maximum speed with which an unpowered car of mass 1000 kg can take a corner of radius 20 m if the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road is 0.5. Take g = 10 ms −2 . —

A coin is pushed down tangentially from an angular position θ on a cylindrical surface, with a velocity v as shown in the figure. If the coefficient of friction between the coin and the surface is μ, find the tangential acceleration of the coin. —

A pendulum consists of a light string of length 25 cm and a small bob of mass 150 g. It is set into motion so that it makes 90 rpm as a conical pendulum. Calculate the ratio of increase in kinetic energy to the increase in gravitational potential energy of the bob. (Take π = 22/7) —

answer: c the necessary centripetal force is obtained from the horizontal component of the normal reaction
stem: Railway tracks are banked at the curves so that: (a) the train may not fall down inwards (b) the weight of the train may be reduced (c) the necessary centripetal force may be obtained from the horizontal component of the reaction of the train (d) no frictional force may be produced between the wheel and the track
book_key: c the necessary centripetal force may be obtained from the horizontal component of the reaction

answer: a the inner wheel leaves the ground first
stem: A car sometimes overturns while taking a turn. When it overturns, it is: (a) the inner wheel which leaves the ground first (b) the outer wheel which leaves the ground first (c) both the wheels leave the ground simultaneously (d) either wheel which leaves the ground first
book_key: a the inner wheel which leaves the ground first

answer: a radius of curvature of outer rail greater than inner rail
stem: A train is moving towards north. At one place it turns towards north-east. Here, we observe that: (a) the radius of curvature of outer rail will be greater than that of the inner rail (b) the radius of curvature of the inner rail will be greater than that of outer rail (c) the radius of curvature of one of the rails will be greater (d) the radius of curvature of the outer and inner rails will be the same
book_key: a the radius of curvature of the outer rail will be greater than that of the inner rail

stem: The outer rail of the curved railway track is raised above the inner one: (a) to provide centripetal force (b) to overcome the frictional force (c) to balance the gravity (d) for some reason other than those mentioned above
A cyclist turns around a curve at 40 km/hr. If it rounds the curve at double the speed, its tendency to overturn is: (a) doubled (b) tripled (c) halved (d) quadrupled
A 2 kg object is rotating at 3 rad/s at a radius of 0.5 m. What is the centrifugal force? (a) 9 N (b) 6 N (c) 7.5 N (d) 3 N

The radius of curvature of a railway line at a place when the train is moving with a speed of 36 kmh −1 is 1000 m, the distance between the two rails being 1.5 metre. Calculate the elevation of the outer rail above the inner rail so that there may be no side pressure on the rails (in m).

A metal ring of mass m and radius R is placed on a smooth horizontal table and is set rotating about its own axis in such a way that each part of the ring moves with a speed υ. The tension in the ring mv 2 /(xπR), find x.

A car is negotiating a curve of radius 150 m with a speed of 15 ms −1 . The angle through which the pendulum suspended from the top of the ceiling would deviate is: (g = 10 ms −2 ) (a) tan −1 (3/20) (b) tan −1 (5/16) (c) tan −1 (4/15) (d) tan −1 (3/16)

A car is moving on a circular level road of curvature 300 metres. If the coefficient of friction is 0.3 and acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s 2 , the maximum speed the car can have is: (a) 30 km/hr (b) 81 km/hr (c) 108 km/hr (d) 162 km/hr
A cyclist goes round a circular track 630 m long in 20 second. What is the angle (in degree) that his cycle makes with the vertical to safely cover the circular track?

A small particle of mass 0.36 g rests on a horizontal turntable at a distance 25 cm from the axis of spindle. The turntable is accelerated at a rate of α = (1/3) rad s −2 . The frictional force that the table exerts on the particle 2 s after the startup is: (a) 40 μN (b) 30 μN (c) 50 μN (d) 60 μN

A car travels with constant speed on a circular road on level ground. In the diagram, F air is the force of air resistance on the car. Which of the other forces shown best represents the horizontal force of the road on the car’s tires? (a) F A (b) F B (c) F C (d) F D
book_key: b F B — inward (centripetal) plus forward (to cancel F air )

answer: b, c (g sinθ = (v²/r)cosθ and N sinθ = mv²/r)
stem: A ball of mass m is rotating in a circle of radius r with speed v inside a smooth cone as shown in figure. Let N be the normal reaction on the ball by the cone, then choose the correct option. (a) N = mg cosθ (b) g sinθ = (v²/r) cosθ (c) N sinθ − mv²/r = 0 (d) None of these
book_key: b, c Both (b) and (c) are correct — (a) is not ⚠

stem: A mass of 2 kg is whirled in a horizontal circle by means of a string at an initial speed of 5 revolutions per minute. Keeping the radius constant, the tension in the string is doubled. The new speed is nearly: (a) 14 rpm (b) 10 rpm (c) 2.25 rpm (d) 7 rpm

What is the greatest speed (in m/s) at which a car having a tract of 1.5 m can turn in a circular path of radius 24.5 m without overturning? Assume that the centre of gravity of the car is 0.49 m above the ground.

A car is moving in a circular path of radius 50 m on a rough horizontal ground; the mass of the car is 1000 kg. At a certain moment when the speed of the car is 5 ms −1 the driver is increasing speed at the rate of 1 ms −2 , then the value of static friction at this moment is (500√x) N. Find x.

A particle describes a horizontal circle in a conical funnel whose inner surface is smooth with speed of 0.5 m/s. What is the height of the plane of circle from vertex of the funnel. (a) 0.25 m (b) 2 cm (c) 4 cm (d) 2.5 cm

answer: b N ⊥ incline, friction up the slope
stem: A car is travelling on a banked road with a speed of 10 m/s on a banked road of inclination 37° in a circle of radius 30 m. The car does not skid. The correct free body diagram of car is: (a) [figure: N ⊥ incline, f down the incline] (b) [figure: N ⊥ incline, f up the incline] (c) [figure: N vertical, f up the incline] (d) [figure: N ⊥ incline, f up the incline and an extra horizontal f]
book_key: b (b) — N ⊥ incline and friction UP the slope (v = 10 m/s < v 0 = 15 m/s)

stem: A car speeds up with constant magnitude of tangential acceleration in a circular path moving in anticlockwise direction. Which of the following figure represents acceleration of the car? (a) [figure] (b) [figure] (c) [figure] (d) [figure]
book_key: c (c) — every arrow points inward and tilted forward (anticlockwise)

stem: An automobile of mass m is going around a curve in an arc of a circle of radius R at a speed v. The curve is banked at an angle θ to the horizontal and the coefficient of static friction between the tires and the road is μ s . If θ is not very big, the maximum speed the car can be moving without skidding is? (a) √[gR(sinθ+μ s cosθ)/(cosθ−μ s sinθ)] (b) √[gR(cosθ+μ s sinθ)/(cosθ−μ s sinθ)] (c) √[mgR(sinθ+μ s cosθ)/(sinθ−μ s cosθ)] (d) √[gR(cosθ+μ s sinθ)/(sinθ−μ s cosθ)]
book_key: a √[gR(sinθ + μ s cosθ)/(cosθ − μ s sinθ)]

stem: Multiple Correct Answer Question.
